messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — increased error rate from serving runtime (cuda illegal memory access). paging oncall. priority=P1 :rotating_light:

sylvie: i'm onpager. seeing repeated CUDA illegal memory access errors across several pods in us-east-1, cluster rw-inference-prod. requests are failing with 500s.

raj: acked, joining. which model/pool?

sylvie: mostly on 'rwd-medium-v2' pods on node g-rw-inference-03. CPU fine but GPU logs show mem access faults.

maria: pulling dmesg from node, one sec.

maria: pastebin of kernel logs: 
```
[ 234567.890123] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, pid=4213, src=u32, ctx=0x1a2b
[ 234567.890456] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 234567.891000] kernel: [drm] nvidia: GPU lockup - trying to recover
[ 234568.000345] serve[4213]: runtime error: CUDA illegal memory access at address 0x7f8a1b2c3d4e
```

kevin: same Xid 79 often surfaces when there are kernel/driver races or misaligned accesses from kernels. could be model kvcache bug or a concurrency race in our custom CUDA kernels.

jordan: customer-impact: initial metrics show ~7% of p95 requests are failing in the last 12m, two customers experiencing degraded throughput. CS alerted.

sylvie: mitigation idea: drain g-rw-inference-03 and route new traffic away, scale up standby nodes in eu/west to take load. can we toggle fallback to fp16-quantized variant for affected routes?

raj: starting node drain: `kubectl cordon g-rw-inference-03 && kubectl drain g-rw-inference-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook step triggered: fallback-routing -> enable. Confirm to proceed with routing change? (react with :thumbsup: to confirm)

maria: collecting container logs while drain starts: most pods crash with stack containing our custom attention kernel call.

kevin: temporary mitigation: update routing policy to prefer 'rwd-medium-v2-q4' (quantized) for 80% of traffic, keep 20% on original for regression monitoring. applying now.

raj: routing change applied, verifying... traffic shift looks good; error rate dropped to 1.2% within 3m.

jordan: updating customers: "We're actively mitigating GPU runtime errors; we've shifted to a quantized variant and are draining a problematic node. Expecting reduced errors in 10-20 minutes."

maria: node drain complete, all pods evicted. kubelet reports one pod terminated with SIGILL before eviction.

kevin: i'm attaching a short repro stack from the failing container: 
```
#0  0x7f8a1b2c in cuLaunchKernel+0x24
#1  0x7f8a2c3d in custom_attention_forward+0xb4
#2  0x7f8a3d4e in ServeModel::forward
```

kevin: looks like our custom kernel is hitting a race when kvcache is shared across streams. will open an urgent PR to serialize access.

sylvie: for now we've drained the node and prevented new scheduling there. can we restart the NVIDIA driver on the drained node and repro in a controlled canary?

raj: i'm repro-ing on a staging instance with the same driver (535.xx) and model. i can reproduce the illegal memory access within ~50 runs. collecting nvprof traces.

kevin: note — upgrading driver in prod is risky mid-incident. prefer to isolate by node and patch kernel code first. i will push a guarded serialization patch to the attention kernel and create a canary build.

maria: CS wants timeline and which customers impacted. jordan, can you share IDs?

jordan: customers: AcmeCorp (realtime embeddings), Skylark (chat), OmegaLabs (batch). notifying their CSMs now.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled in 30m. Current oncall: sylvie -> incoming: oliver. Add notes to incident channel.

sylvie: handoff summary for oliver:
- incident: CUDA illegal memory access (Xid 79 / GPU lockup) on g-rw-inference-03 causing 5-8% request failures
- immediate mitigations: drained node, shifted 80% traffic to quantized model variant, restarted affected pods on other nodes, customer CS notified
- ongoing work: kevin reproducing locally, patching kernel to add serialization around kvcache, raj validating canary, maria collecting full nvprof and dmesg bundles
- risk: potential regression in latency/quality from quantized variant; monitor model-level evals and p95 latency
- next steps: if canary passes, coordinated rollout of patched model binary to remaining nodes; if canary fails, fallback to dedicated-host pool or further isolate on different driver version

raj: canary runs passed with patched kernel for 200 consecutive requests, no illegal access observed. preparing canary deployment to prod-safe pool (two nodes).

kevin: PR -> 8472 created with guarded locks around kvcache access. cc @sylvie for review. will include microbenchmark numbers.

maria: pack logs and attach to ticket IN-2025-437. nvprof traces show memory write at offset misaligned by 8 bytes occasionally. looks like pointer math bug in reduce kernel.

jordan: CS updated the customers with a technical summary and ETA 4 hours for full remediation.

sylvie: handing off now — leaving open for follow-up. oliver please take over in 30m. main action items: monitor p95 / error-rate, validate canary rollout, coordinate postmortem (owner: kevin).

oliver: thanks, taking over. will post handoff note and keep everyone updated. :ok_hand:
